title: The Success of Acquisitions: Evidence from Divestitures

rival_explanations: the higher divestiture rate of diversifying acquisitions is an artifact of shorter elapsed time since related acquisitions were completed (age rather than relatedness)

the large difference in divestiture rates reflects non-performance-based causes (integration cost and relaxed antitrust / deconglomeration) rather than diversifying acquisitions being worse investments

context.time_period: acquisitions completed 1971-1982, divestitures tracked through end of 1989
context.sample_description: Large acquisitions from Mergers and Acquisitions magazine's lists of the largest completed deals; restricted to transactions valued at least $100 million in 1982 dollars, excluding foreign, insurance, bank, and railroad acquirers, requiring acquirer stock-return data on the CRSP tapes, and requiring target purchase price to exceed 5% of acquirer equity market value
